text:
vendor-streamlineops: heads up — StreamlineOps detected a public S3 bucket that contained daily debug logs from their service. They say it included some request IDs that map to our tenant IDs. Vendor provided link: https://status.streamlineops.example/incident/452 (they claim no creds leaked).

maria_g: thanks — do we know which tenant IDs/path prefixes are mentioned? can someone search our ingest logs for those request IDs?

akash: listing the IDs from their report now. give me a minute.

akash: quick check: one request-id appears in cloudfront access logs for our hosted-api gateway between 2025-03-10T02:00 and 02:30 UTC. Not seeing any auth tokens in their snippet, looks like path + query params only. :thinking_face:

jordan_sre: ok, immediate questions: 1) any customer PII in those logs? 2) were any of our KMS-encrypted payloads exposed in plaintext? 3) do RBAC tokens rotate?

maria_g: vendor says logs are application debug logs — may include user emails in URI in a few cases. vendor also says they redacted tokens but might have full URLs.

sec-bot: automated note — created incident INC-20250310-452, severity: medium, assigned: eng-security.

jordan_sre: containment steps we should do now: 1) request vendor to take the bucket offline and provide a retention snapshot; 2) confirm list of exposed keys/IDs; 3) rotate any downstream integration credentials we have with them; 4) run targeted search for PII in our logs.

maria_g: contacting StreamlineOps CISO and support lead. cc @legal_ops.

legal_ops: put on our legal review queue. we need vendor's attestation and timeline before customer comms. also check contract for breach notification SLA.

akash: ran a grep over parsed logs for patterns that look like emails and tenant IDs for the window. small number (~12 hits) — redacted here: 5 customer emails matched internal test accounts, 7 matched production tenant IDs. No 36-char API keys or JWTs found in stored logs snippet.

jordan_sre: good. next: verify KMS-wrapped artifacts. akash — can you run this quick query against our object metadata store?

akash: running: ```aws s3api list-objects-v2 --bucket redwood-ingest-logs --prefix=2025/03/10/ | jq '.Contents[] | select(.Key|test("(request-id-123|request-id-456)"))'``` will take ~2m

akash: result: matching objects are encrypted with AES256 server-side and reference KMS key arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01. No plaintext payloads present in S3.

maria_g: vendor responded: bucket taken offline, they shared a sanitized archive and commit hash for logs. they also offered root-cause was a misapplied IAM policy during a deploy.

jordan_sre: action items: - vendor to provide full list of exposed object keys and hashes - we rotate integration API key + reissue client cert for the connector - run full PII scan for last 90 days on our ingress logs - legal to prepare customer notification template (if required) - create post-incident evaluation to tighten RBAC on vendor onboarding

maria_g: assigning: akash -> log scan & KMS verification, jordan_sre -> coordinate rotations + infra mitigations, legal_ops -> contract/notice, sec-bot -> track tasks in INC-20250310-452.

akash: note on rotations — our connector uses a service principal with a scoped API key. I'll revoke and rotate, update vault: ```vault kv put secret/vendors/streamlineops api_key=REDACTED expiry=2025-03-11```

jordan_sre: also enable additional audit logging on our side for all vendor-related routes for 30 days. add a canary alert for unusual volume of auth failures.

legal_ops: drafting a fact-based notice to customers affected by the tenant IDs found. will circulate in #all-hands-cust-comms for review.

vendor-streamlineops: confirming we have provided the full file manifest and will share S3 access logs for the exposed bucket. we apologize — root cause was human error in a terraform apply. we will run an IAM policy audit and share remediation actions.

maria_g: please include your rotated credentials/certs timeline and who had access. we need proof of deletion and a signed statement for our compliance record.

sec-bot: update — actions logged: 6 tasks created, SLA: 72h for vendor attestation.

jordan_sre: post-incident checklist draft (short): 1) Confirm deletion + attestation from vendor 2) Confirm no plaintext KMS material leaked 3) Rotate our integration creds 4) Run 90-day PII scan, share results 5) Update vendor onboarding RBAC checklist 6) Customer notice if any production tenant PII confirmed

akash: starting the 90-day scan now. ETA ~4h. will post a summary and redacted hits.

maria_g: thanks all. will keep this thread for updates. if anyone finds evidence of keys or more PII, ping immediately and escalate to Sev2. :exclamation:
